title: Geely EX5, EX2 & Starray EM-I 36-Month Finance: $0 Deposit, 0.68% P.a. Comp Rate + 1000kwh Public Charging Credit with Trade-in
body:
Deal: Geely EX5, EX2 & Starray EM-I 36-Month Finance: $0 Deposit, 0.68% P.a. Comp Rate + 1000kwh Public Charging Credit with Trade-in

[Ryanek] They've been making EV's for 18 years and are 8th in global sales.
They've grown 78% in three years. I don't think they're going anywhere.
[Wiadro] powered by the Chinese government subsidies on ev's
[Big L] Like every other government subsidised car manufacturers, except ours
[gguu] I think there is a loan establishing fee about $1500 which needs to be taken into account
upd: "a dealer origination fee which is charged by your dealer and could be up to $1,495"
[letmethefuqin] This is correct. 0.68% over 3 years plus a $1500 establishment fee.
[SKS01] In that case, p.a. is not 0.68% since p.a. must include all fees.
National Credit Code, Section 157(3): The comparison rate will reflect the total cost of credit arising from interest charges and other prescribed credit fees and charges.
https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/nccpa…
[Matt P] Driveaway pricing on EX2 was a better deal. Now they're offering financing that a large chunk of the market won't want to take up (favouring $0 FBT novated leases).
[shxhshzhz] There has never been a driveaway price deal for the Geely EX2
[Legendalvin] Did anyone manage to get a good driveaway price through negotiation ? Aside from accessories, I wonder if cash discount is negotiable
[letmethefuqin] Cash isnt going to change anything
Sales guys make basically nothing off these
Thats what the establishment fee of $1500 basically is.
[Recollect9764] To be fair they also offer 6% off for novated leases

[ymmf] Didn't they have 0.09% not long ago? So it's a worse deal than before?
